Theme

Playground equipment, sandbox toys, vehicles and play

weight-lifting noun and verb

also weightlifting, lift weights, weights, do weights

modern

Traupman 51, 405

sublātiō lībrāmentōrum

Traupman’s phrase. Both words are classical: sublātiō, a lifting (Quint.), and lībrāmentum, a weight (lībrāmentum plumbī, Liv. 42.63.4). Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

Other words

  • lībrāmenta tollere

    also used · modern · Traupman 60, 64

    lībrāmentum is classically a weight that presses down (plumbī, Liv. 42.63.4, Lewis & Short). Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

  • halterēs, halterum m. pl. — hand weights, dumb-bells

    noun, third declension, plural · also used · classical · Mart. 14.49.1 (Lewis & Short s.v. halter); Mart. 7.67.6 (Lewis & Short)

    The Greek athlete’s lead weights, held in the hands (Lewis & Short: “the dumb-bells of modern gymnastics”); the word for the weights themselves.

See also gym, exercise.
